key_insight: HASTE makes rapid post-disaster building damage assessment accessible to non-ML users by turning satellite imagery into per-building damage maps through a no-code web platform. It is designed for the critical first hours after a disaster, when matched imagery and task-specific training data are usually unavailable.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the urgent need to quickly identify which buildings are damaged after a disaster, without relying on idealized benchmark conditions or a team of machine learning engineers.
method: Provides a no-code web platform for analysts to generate damage assessments from satellite imagery.
Supports rapid, per-building mapping of damage for new disaster events where before-and-after image pairs may be incomplete or unavailable.
Focuses on operational usability so responders can create actionable maps within hours of an event.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how disaster-response systems can move beyond benchmark performance toward real-world deployment constraints. It highlights the value of human-centered tooling, robustness to data mismatch, and practical workflows for emergency response.

paper_title: HASTE: A Platform for Rapid Post-Disaster Building Damage Assessment
paper_authors: Caleb Robinson, Anthony Ortiz, Simone Fobi Nsutezo, Cameron Birge, Meygha Machado
